question: What did the hypocrites say when a calamity overtook the Prophet?
answer: They said 'We took our precaution beforehand' (meaning they took precautions when they did not join him), and they turned away rejoicing.
reasoning_span: وَإِن تُصِبْكَ مُصِيبَةٌ يَقُولُواْ قَدْ أَخَذْنَا أَمْرَنَا مِن قَبْلُ (but if a calamity overtakes you, they say: "We took our precaution beforehand,"), they say, we took precautions when we did not join him, وَيَتَوَلَّواْ وَّهُمْ فَرِحُونَ (and they turn away rejoicing.)

question: According to the tafsir of Surah 9:50, what does the Prophet say in reply to the hypocrites' enmity?
answer: The Prophet says: 'Nothing shall ever happen to us except what Allah has ordained for us. He is our Mawla (Master and protector), and in Allah let the believers put their trust.'
reasoning_span: لَّن يُصِيبَنَآ إِلاَّ مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَنَا (Nothing shall ever happen to us except what Allah has ordained for us.) for we are under His control and decree, هُوَ مَوْلَـنَا (He is our Mawla.), Master and protector

question: Which hadith did Imam Ahmad record about reading Surah At-Takwir (81)?
answer: Ibn Umar narrated that the Messenger of Allah said: 'Whoever wishes to look at the Day of Judgement as if he is seeing it with his own eyes, then let him read (When the sun is wound round.), (When the heaven is cleft asunder.) and (When the heaven is split asunder.)'
reasoning_span: Imam Ahmad recorded from Ibn `Umar that the Messenger of Allah said, «مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يَنْظُرَ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ كَأَنَّهُ رَأْيُ عَيْنٍ فَلْيَقْرَأْ: إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ» (Whoever wishes to look at the Day of Judgement as if he is seeing it with his own eyes, then let him read, (When the sun is wound round.))

question: What does 'Kuwwirat' mean according to Ibn Abbas in the tafsir of Surah At-Takwir?
answer: According to Ali bin Abi Talhah's report from Ibn Abbas, Kuwwirat means the sun 'will be darkened.' Al-Awfi reported from Ibn Abbas that it means 'it will go away.'
reasoning_span: `Ali bin Abi Talhah reported from Ibn `Abbas: إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ (When the sun is Kuwwirat.) "This means it will be darkened." Al-`Awfi reported from Ibn `Abbas; "It will go away."

question: What hadith did Al-Bukhari record about the sun and moon on the Day of Judgement?
answer: Al-Bukhari recorded from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet said: 'The sun and the moon will be rolled up on the Day of Judgement.'
reasoning_span: Al-Bukhari recorded from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet said, «الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ يُكَوَّرَانِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَة» (The sun and the moon will be rolled up on the Day of Judgement.)

question: What are Al-Ishar (pregnant she-camels) and why will they be neglected according to the tafsir of Surah 81?
answer: Al-Ishar are pregnant she-camels that have reached the tenth month of pregnancy — considered the best type of camel. They will be neglected because people will be too busy to tend to, take care of, or benefit from them, due to the great, terrifying, and horrible situation of the Day of Judgement.
reasoning_span: the `Ishar is a type of camel. It is actually the best type of camel, and particularly the pregnant females of them when they have reached the tenth month of their pregnancies... So the people will be too busy to tend to her, take care of her or benefit from her, after she used to be the most important thing to them. This will be due to what will suddenly overtake them of the great, terrifying and horrible situation.

question: What does 'Nufsus Zuwwijat' (souls are joined with their mates) mean according to the tafsir of Surah 81?
answer: It means every type of soul will be gathered with its peer or mate. The Prophet explained it means 'every man will be with every group of people who performed the same deeds that he did.'
reasoning_span: وَإِذَا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ (And when the souls are joined with their mates.) meaning, every type (of soul) will be gathered with its peer (or mate).

question: Why will the female infant buried alive (Al-Maw'udah) be questioned on the Day of Judgement?
answer: She will be questioned about what sin she committed that caused her to be murdered. This will be a means of frightening her murderer — for if the one who was wronged is questioned, the wrongdoer will face an even greater reckoning.
reasoning_span: on the Day of Judgement, the female infant will be asked what sin she committed that caused here to be murdered. This will be a means of frightening her murderer. For verily, if the one who was wronged is questioned, what does the wrongdoer (the one who is guilty of the oppression) think then

question: What did the Prophet say about coitus interruptus (withdrawal) in relation to Al-Maw'udah?
answer: The Prophet said: 'That is the minor infanticide and it is the female infant buried alive (Maw'udah) that will be questioned.'
reasoning_span: «ذلِكَ الْوَأْدُ الْخَفِيُّ، وَهُوَ الْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَت» (That is the minor infanticide and it is the female infant buried alive (Maw'udah) that will be questioned.)

question: What did Qays bin Asim ask the Prophet about having buried his daughters alive, and what was the Prophet's response?
answer: Qays bin Asim came to the Prophet and said he had buried some daughters alive in pre-Islamic ignorance. The Prophet said: 'Free a slave for each one of them.' When Qays said he owned camels instead, the Prophet said: 'Then sacrifice a camel for each one of them.'
reasoning_span: "Qays bin `Asim came to the Messenger of Allah and said, `O Messenger of Allah! Verily, I buried some daughters of mine alive in the period of pre-Islamic ignorance.' The Messenger of Allah said, «أَعْتِقْ عَنْ كُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ رَقَبَة» (Free a slave for each one of them.)

question: According to the tafsir of Surah 18:98, what did Dhul-Qarnayn say the barrier was?
answer: Dhul-Qarnayn said the barrier was 'a mercy from my Lord' for the people, as it stopped Ya'juj and Ma'juj from spreading evil and corruption on earth.
reasoning_span: قَالَ هَـذَا رَحْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّى (He said: This is a mercy from my Lord) for the people, when he placed a barrier between them and Ya'juj and Ma'juj, to stop them from spreading evil and corruption on earth.

question: What hadith did Imam Ahmad record from Zaynab bint Jahsh about the barrier of Ya'juj and Ma'juj?
answer: Zaynab bint Jahsh reported that the Prophet woke from sleep red in the face and said: 'La ilaha illallah! Woe to the Arabs from the evil that has approached (them). Today a hole has been opened in the barrier of Ya'juj and Ma'juj like this,' making a circle with his index finger and thumb.
reasoning_span: Imam Ahmad recorded that Zaynab bint Jahsh, the wife of the Prophet said, "The Prophet woke from sleep, and he was red in the face. He said, «لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَيْلٌ لِلْعَرَبِ مِنْ شَرَ قَدِ اقْتَرَبَ فُتِحَ الْيَوْمَ مِنْ رَدْمِ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ مِثْلُ هَذَا» (La ilaha illallah! Woe to the Arabs from the evil that has approached (them). Today a hole has been opened in the barrier of Ya'juj and Ma'juj like this.) and he made a circle with his index finger and thumb.

question: What does the word 'Dakka' mean in Arabic according to the tafsir of Surah 18:98?
answer: The Arabs use Dakka' to describe a female camel whose back is flat and has no hump, meaning 'level to the ground.'
reasoning_span: The Arabs use Dakka' to describe a female camel whose back is flat and has no hump. And Allah says: فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّى رَبُّهُ لِلْجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُ دَكًّا (So when his Lord appeared to the mountain, He made it Dakkan) 7:143 meaning, level to the ground.

question: According to Surah 6:121, what is the ruling on eating food over which Allah's Name has not been mentioned?
answer: It is not lawful to eat such food. The Ayah states that eating what Allah's Name has not been mentioned over is 'grave disobedience' (fisq), and the tafsir confirms this is used as proof that slaughtered animals are not lawful when Allah's Name is not mentioned over them.
reasoning_span: This Ayah is used to prove that slaughtered animals are not lawful when Allah's Name is not mentioned over them -- even if slaughtered by a Muslim.

question: What hadith about hunting dogs is mentioned in the tafsir of Surah 6:121?
answer: The hadith from Adi bin Hatim and Abu Tha'labah states: 'When you send your trained hunting dog and mention Allah's Name on releasing it, then eat from whatever it catches for you.' This was collected in the Two Sahihs.
reasoning_span: «إِذَا أَرْسَلْتَ كَلْبَكَ الْمُعَلَّمَ وَذَكْرتَ اسْمَ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ فَكُلْ مَا أَمْسَكَ عَلَيْك» (When you send your trained hunting dog and mention Allah's Name on releasing it, then eat from whatever it catches for you.) This Hadith was collected in the Two Sahihs.

question: What does the tafsir of Surah 6:121 say about obeying the disbelievers who call for eating dead animals?
answer: The tafsir states that obeying them in eating dead animals constitutes Shirk (polytheism), as giving preference to anyone's saying over Allah's legislation is Shirk.
reasoning_span: وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ (and if you obey them, then you would indeed be polytheists.) means, when you turn away from Allah's command and Legislation to the saying of anyone else, preferring other than what Allah has said, then this constitutes Shirk.

question: What is the meaning of the Ayah in Surah 39:38 'Sufficient for me is Allah'?
answer: It means 'Allah is enough for me.' The Prophet also elaborated: 'Know that even if the entire nation were to come together to do you some harm that Allah has not decreed for you, they will never be able to harm you.'
reasoning_span: قُلْ حَسْبِىَ اللَّهُ (Say: "Sufficient for me is Allah...") means, `Allah is enough for me.'

question: In the tafsir of Surah 39:38, what lengthy hadith is recorded from Ibn Abbas attributed to the Prophet about relying on Allah?
answer: The hadith says: 'Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you; be mindful of Allah and you will find Him ever with you. Turn to Allah in times of ease and He will turn to you in times of difficulty... Know that even if the entire nation were to come together to do you some harm that Allah has not decreed for you, they will never be able to harm you... The pages have dried and the pens have been lifted... know that in patiently persevering with regard to something that you dislike there is much goodness. Victory comes with patience, a way out comes from difficulty and with hardship comes ease.'
reasoning_span: «احْفَظِ اللهَ يَحْفَظْكَ، احْفَظِ اللهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَكَ، تَعَرَّفْ إِلَى اللهِ فِي الرَّخَاءِ يَعْرِفْكَ فِي الشِّدَّةِ، إِذَا سَأَلْتَ فَاسْأَلِ اللهَ، وَإِذَا اسْتَعَنْتَ فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللهِ، وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْأُمَّةَ لَوِ اجْتَمَعُوا عَلى أَنْ يَضُرُّوكَ بِشَيْءٍ لَمْ يَكْتُبْهُ اللهُ عَلَيْكَ لَمْ يَضُرُّوكَ»

question: What did the Jews say when the Ayah about lending to Allah was revealed, according to the tafsir of Surah 3:181?
answer: When the Ayah 'Who is he that will lend to Allah a goodly loan' (2:245) was revealed, the Jews said: 'O Muhammad! Has your Lord become poor so that He asks His servants to give Him a loan?'
reasoning_span: Sa`id bin Jubayr said that Ibn `Abbas said, "When Allah's statement, مَّن ذَا الَّذِى يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا (Who is he that will lend to Allah a goodly loan so that He may multiply it to him many times) 2:245 was revealed, the Jews said, `O Muhammad! Has your Lord become poor so that He asks His servants to give Him a loan?'

question: What is the meaning of 'those who made angels females' in Surah 43:19?
answer: The idolators believed the angels were females (daughters of Allah). Allah denounces this saying they did not witness the creation of the angels as females. Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned about it on the Day of Resurrection.
reasoning_span: وَجَعَلُواْ الْمَلَـئِكَةَ الَّذِينَ هُمْ عِبَادُ الرَّحْمَـنِ إِنَـثاً (And they make females the angels who themselves are servants of the Most Gracious.) means, that is what they believe about them, but Allah denounces them for that and says: أَشَهِدُواْ خَلْقَهُمْ (Did they witness their creation) meaning, did they see Allah creating them as females

question: What is the meaning of 'Qawwamun' (protectors and maintainers) in Surah 4:34 according to the tafsir?
answer: It means the man is responsible for the woman, and he is her maintainer, caretaker and leader who disciplines her if she deviates. This is because men excel over women for certain tasks, and because men spend from their wealth on women.
reasoning_span: الرِّجَالُ قَوَّامُونَ عَلَى النِّسَآءِ (Men are the protectors and maintainers of women,) meaning, the man is responsible for the woman, and he is her maintainer, caretaker and leader who disciplines her if she deviates.

question: What hadith did the Prophet say about appointing a woman as a leader, according to the tafsir of Surah 4:34?
answer: The Prophet said: 'People who appoint a woman to be their leader, will never achieve success.' This was recorded by Al-Bukhari.
reasoning_span: The Prophet said, «لَنْ يُفْلِحَ قَوْمٌ وَلَّوْا أَمْرَهُمُ امْرَأَة» (People who appoint a woman to be their leader, will never achieve success.) Al-Bukhari recorded this Hadith.

question: What are the three steps a husband may take when facing his wife's ill-conduct (nushuz) according to Surah 4:34?
answer: The three steps are: (1) admonish/advise her, (2) abandon her in bed, and (3) beat her (lightly, without severe beating).
reasoning_span: Allah's statement, وَاللَّـتِى تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ (As to those women on whose part you see ill conduct, admonish them (first)). Allah's statement, وَاهْجُرُوهُنَّ فِى الْمَضَاجِعِ (abandon them in their beds,)... وَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ (beat them) means, if advice and ignoring her in the bed do not produce the desired results, you are allowed to discipline the wife, without severe beating.

question: According to the tafsir of Surah 4:34, what hadith warns about a wife refusing her husband's bed?
answer: Al-Bukhari recorded from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet said: 'If the man asks his wife to come to his bed and she declines, the angels will keep cursing her until the morning.'
reasoning_span: Al-Bukhari recorded that Abu Hurayrah said that the Messenger of Allah said, «إِذَا دَعَا الرَّجُلُ امْرَأَتَهُ إِلى فِرَاشِهِ فَأَبَتْ عَلَيْهِ، لَعَنَتْهَا الْمَلَائِكَةُ حَتَّى تُصْبِح» (If the man asks his wife to come to his bed and she declines, the angels will keep cursing her until the morning.)

question: What did Sulayman (Solomon) ask from Allah after being tested, according to the tafsir of Surah 38:35?
answer: Sulayman said: 'My Lord! Forgive me, and bestow upon me a kingdom such as shall not belong to any other after me. Verily, You are the Bestower.'
reasoning_span: قَالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِى وَهَبْ لِى مُلْكاً لاَّ يَنبَغِى لاًّحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِى إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْوَهَّابُ (He said: "My Lord! Forgive me, and bestow upon me a kingdom such as shall not belong to any other after me. Verily, You are the Bestower.")

question: What hadith did Al-Bukhari record from Abu Hurayrah about Sulayman's prayer in the context of Surah 38:35?
answer: The Prophet said that an Ifrit (powerful jinn) tried to interrupt his prayer, but Allah enabled him to overpower it. He wanted to tie it to a pillar of the masjid, but then remembered Sulayman's prayer: 'My Lord! Forgive me and bestow upon me a kingdom such as shall not belong to any other after me.'
reasoning_span: «إِنَّ عِفْرِيتًا مِنَ الْجِنِّ تَفَلَّتَ عَلَيَّ الْبَارِحَةَ... فَذَكَرْتُ قَوْلَ أَخِي سُلَيْمَانَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِى وَهَبْ لِى مُلْكاً لاَّ يَنبَغِى لاًّحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِى» (An `Ifrit from among the Jinn came and bothered me last night... Then I remembered what my brother Sulayman said, (My Lord! Forgive me and bestow upon me a kingdom such as shall not belong to any other after me))

question: What does the tafsir say about the bedouins' (Al-A'rab) disbelief and hypocrisy in Surah 9:97?
answer: The tafsir states that the disbelief and hypocrisy of the bedouins is worse and deeper than that of others, and they are the most likely to be ignorant of the commandments that Allah has revealed to His Messenger.
reasoning_span: Allah states that there are disbelievers, hypocrites and believers among the bedouins. He also states that the disbelief and hypocrisy of the bedouins is worse and deeper than the disbelief and hypocrisy of others. They are the most likely of being ignorant of the commandments that Allah has revealed to His Messenger.

question: What hadith does the tafsir mention about a person who lives in the desert, according to Surah 9:97?
answer: Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of Allah said: 'He who lives in the desert becomes hard-hearted, he who follows the game becomes heedless, and he who associates with the rulers falls into Fitnah.'
reasoning_span: Imam Ahmad narrated that Ibn `Abbas said that the Messenger of Allah said, «مَنْ سَكَنَ الْبَادِيَةَ جَفَا، وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ الصَّيْدَ غَفَلَ، وَمَنْ أَتَى السُّلْطَانَ افْتُتِن» (He who lives in the desert becomes hard-hearted, he who follows the game becomes heedless, and he who associates with the rulers falls into Fitnah.)

question: According to Surah 19:81, what do the disbelievers expect from the idols they worship?
answer: They took gods besides Allah so that these gods would be a source of honor and might for them, thinking the gods would give them power and make them victorious.
reasoning_span: Allah, the Exalted, informs about the disbelievers who associate partners with their Lord, that they have taken gods besides Allah, so that these gods may be a source of honor and might for them. They think that these gods give them power and make them victorious.

question: What will happen to the idols on the Day of Judgement according to Surah 19:81?
answer: The idols will deny the worship of their worshippers and will become their adversaries, in a state contrary to what the worshippers had hoped.
reasoning_span: Allah mentions that the matter is not as they claim, and it will not be as they hope. He says, كَلاَّ سَيَكْفُرُونَ بِعِبَـدَتِهِمْ (Nay, but they will deny their worship of them,) on the Day of Judgement. وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدّاً (and will become their adversaries.) This means that they will be foes in a state other than what they think about these gods.

question: In the story of Ibrahim breaking the idols (Surah 21:63), what did the Prophet say about Ibrahim's three lies?
answer: In the Two Sahihs it is recorded from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet said: 'Ibrahim did not tell lies except on three occasions, two for the sake of Allah — when he said (Nay, this one, the biggest of them did it) and when he said (Verily, I am sick), and the third was regarding Sarah when he called her his sister.'
reasoning_span: In the Two Sahihs it was recorded from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ لَمْ يَكْذِبْ غَيْرَ ثَلَاثٍ: ثِنْتَيْنِ فِي ذَاتِ اللهِ قَوْلُهُ: (Ibrahim, upon him be peace, did not tell lies except on three occasions, two for the sake of Allah -- when he said: بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَـذَا (Nay, this one, the biggest of them did it. ) and when he said: إِنِّى سَقِيمٌ (Verily, I am sick)

question: According to Surah 2:121, what is the meaning of 'Yatlunahu Haqqa Tilawatihi' (reciting it with its true recital)?
answer: According to Ibn Mas'ud: 'The right Tilawah is allowing what it makes lawful, prohibiting what it makes unlawful, reciting it as it was revealed by Allah, not changing the words from their places, and not interpreting it with other than its actual interpretation.'
reasoning_span: Abu Al-`Aliyah said that Ibn Mas`ud said, "By He in Whose Hand is my soul! The right Tilawah is allowing what it makes lawful, prohibiting what it makes unlawful, reciting it as it was revealed by Allah, not changing the words from their places, and not interpreting it with other than its actual interpretation."

question: What hadith is recorded in the Sahih about people of other faiths who hear of the Prophet but do not believe?
answer: The Prophet said: 'By He in Whose Hand is my soul! There is no member of this Ummah (mankind and Jinns), Jew or a Christian, who hears of me, yet does not believe in me, but will enter the Fire.'
reasoning_span: As recorded in the Sahih, the Prophet said, «وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لَا يَسْمَعُ بِي أَحَدٌ مِنْ هذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ يَهُودِيٌّ وَلَا نَصْرَانِيٌّ ثُمَّ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِي إِلَّا دَخَلَ النَّار» (By He in Whose Hand is my soul! There is no member of this Ummah (mankind and Jinns), Jew or a Christian, who hears of me, yet does not believe in me, but will enter the Fire.)

question: Where did Nuh's (Noah's) ship rest after the flood, and what did Qatadah say about it?
answer: The ship rested on Mount Judi. Qatadah said the ship rested on Mount Judi for a month before the people came down from it. He also said Allah made Nuh's ship remain on Mount Judi in the land of Al-Jazirah as a lesson and a sign.
reasoning_span: Qatadah said, "The ship rested upon it (Mount Judi) for a month before they (the people) came down from it." Qatadah also said, "Allah made Nuh's ship remain on Mount Judi in the land of Al-Jazirah, as a lesson and a sign."

question: What does Mujahid say about Mount Judi in the tafsir of Surah 11:44?
answer: Mujahid said that Judi is a mountain in Al-Jazirah (Northwest Mesopotamia). When the flood occurred, all mountains sought to tower above each other, but this mountain humbled itself for Allah, so it was not drowned, and that is why Nuh's ship anchored upon it.
reasoning_span: Mujahid said, "Judi is a mountain in Al-Jazirah (Northwest Mesopotamia) where the mountains sought to tower above each other on the day of the drowning. On that day of destruction, all the mountains sought to be higher (to avoid being overcome by the water). However, this mountain (Judi) humbled itself for Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, and therefore it was not drowned. This is why Nuh's ship anchored upon it."

question: What does the tafsir say about the etiquette of seeking permission to enter houses according to Surah 24:27?
answer: One should seek permission three times before entering. If permission is given, one may enter; otherwise they should go away. The one seeking permission should not stand directly in front of the door but to the right or left.
reasoning_span: This is the Islamic etiquette. Allah taught these manners (of seeking permission) to His believing servants and commanded them not to enter houses other than their own until they had asked permission, i.e., to ask for permission before entering and to give the greeting of Salam after asking. One should seek permission three times, and if permission is given, (he may enter), otherwise he should go away.

question: What is the Islamic ruling about seeking permission to enter upon one's own family members (mahrams) in the house, according to the tafsir of Surah 24:27?
answer: According to Ibn Abbas and Ibn Tawus's father, a man should even seek permission to enter upon his mahram female relatives such as orphan sisters living with him, to avoid seeing them in a state of undress.
reasoning_span: I asked him to make allowances for me but he refused and said, "Do you want to see them naked?" I said, "No." He said, "Then ask for permission to enter."

question: According to the tafsir of Surah 3:32, how is Allah's love attained?
answer: Allah's love is attained by following the way of Muhammad (the Prophet). Whoever follows the Shari'ah of Muhammad in all his statements, actions and conditions will earn Allah's love.
reasoning_span: This honorable Ayah judges against those who claim to love Allah, yet do not follow the way of Muhammad . Such people are not true in their claim until they follow the Shari`ah (Law) of Muhammad and his religion in all his statements, actions and conditions.

question: What does the tafsir of Surah 17:38 say about walking with conceit?
answer: Allah forbids His servants to strut and walk in a boastful manner. The tafsir explains that walking in a boastful manner is acting proud like arrogant oppressors. 'You cannot penetrate the earth with your walking.'
reasoning_span: Allah forbids His servants to strut and walk in a boastful manner: وَلاَ تَمْشِ فِى الاٌّرْضِ مَرَحًا (And walk not on the earth with conceit and arrogance.) meaning, walking in boastful manner and acting proud, like those who are arrogant oppressors.

question: According to the tafsir of Surah 30:15, what will happen to those who believed and did righteous deeds on the Day of Judgement?
answer: They will be in a garden of Paradise, delighted and living a life of luxury.
reasoning_span: فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصَّـلِحَـتِ فَهُمْ فِى رَوْضَةٍ يُحْبَرُونَ (Then as for those who believed and did righteous good deeds, such shall be honored and made to enjoy a luxurious life in a Garden of Delight.) Mujahid and Qatadah said, "This means, they will enjoy a life of luxury."

question: What does Qatadah say about the separation on the Day of Judgement in the tafsir of Surah 30?
answer: Qatadah said: 'By Allah, this refers to the separation after which there will be no reunion.' If one person is taken to the highest heights and another sent to the lowest depths of Hell, that is the last they will ever see of one another.
reasoning_span: Qatadah said: "By Allah, this refers to the separation after which there will be no reunion." In other words, if one person is taken up to the highest heights and another is sent down to the lowest depths of Hell, that is the last they will ever see of one another.

question: What does the tafsir of Surah 55:50 say about the two springs in Paradise?
answer: Al-Hasan Al-Basri said one of the springs is called Tasnim and the other As-Salsabil. Atiyah said the water of one is from non-standing water and the other from wine that gives delight to those who drink it.
reasoning_span: Al-Hasan Al-Basri said that one of these springs is called Tasnim, and the other called As-Salsabil. `Atiyah said that the water of one of these springs is from non-standing water and the other from wine that gives delight to those who drink it.

question: What hadith about the two Gardens of silver and gold in Paradise is mentioned in the tafsir of Surah 55:50?
answer: Al-Bukhari recorded from Abdullah bin Qays that the Prophet said: 'There are two gardens made of silver — their vessels and all that they contain. And there are two gardens made of gold — their vessels and all that they contain. And nothing stands between the people in the Adn Garden and looking at their Lord except the covering of pride before His Face.'
reasoning_span: Al-Bukhari recorded that `Abdullah bin Qays said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, «جَنَّتَانِ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ آنِيَتُهُمَا وَمَا فِيهِمَا، وَجَنَّتَانِ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ آنِيَتُهُمَا وَمَا فِيهِمَا، وَمَا بَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ وَبَيْنَ أَنْ يَنْظُرُوا إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِلَّا رِدَاءُ الْكِبْرِيَاءِ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ فِي جَنَّةِ عَدْن»

question: According to the tafsir of Surah 58:14, the hypocrites were neither with the believers nor with the disbelievers. What Ayah from another Surah confirms this?
answer: Allah said in another Ayah: 'They are swaying between this and that, belonging neither to these nor to those; and he whom Allah sends astray, you will not find for him a way.' (4:143)
reasoning_span: Allah the Exalted said in another Ayah, مُّذَبْذَبِينَ بَيْنَ ذلِكَ لاَ إِلَى هَـؤُلاءِ وَلاَ إِلَى هَـؤُلاءِ وَمَن يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُ سَبِيلاً ((They are) swaying between this and that, belonging neither to these nor to those; and he whom Allah sends astray, you will not find for him a way.)(4:143)

question: What did Abu Dawud record from Abu Ad-Darda about the Shaytan controlling those who do not establish prayer?
answer: Abu Ad-Darda' reported that the Prophet said: 'Any three in a village or desert among whom the Salah is not called for, will have the Shaytan control them. Therefore, adhere to the Jama'ah, for the wolf eats from the strayed sheep.'
reasoning_span: Abu Dawud recorded that Abu Ad-Darda' said that he heard the Messenger of Allah say, «مَا مِنْ ثَلَاثَةٍ فِي قَرْيَةٍ وَلَا بَدْوٍ، لَا تُقَامُ فِيهِمُ الصَّلَاةُ إِلَّا قَدِ اسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطَانُ، فَعَلَيْكَ بِالْجَمَاعَةِ، فَإِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُ الذِّئْبُ الْقَاصِيَة» (Any three in a village or desert among whom the Salah is not called for, will have the Shaytan control them. Therefore, adhere to the Jama`ah, for the wolf eats from the strayed sheep.)

question: According to Surah 10:22, what do people do when they are saved from the storm at sea?
answer: After being saved, they rebel and disobey Allah in the earth wrongfully, as if they had never experienced any difficulties and had never made any promise to Allah.
reasoning_span: فَلَمَّآ أَنجَاهُمْ (But when He delivers them) from that distress, إِذَا هُمْ يَبْغُونَ فِى الاٌّرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ (behold! They rebel (disobey Allah) in the earth wrongfully...) meaning: they returned as if they had never experienced any difficulties and had never promised Him anything.

question: What does Al-Bukhari record about what Allah said after a night of rain, in the tafsir of Surah 10:22?
answer: Al-Bukhari recorded that the Prophet led the Dawn prayer after rain and said: 'Allah said: This morning, some of My servants have become believers and some disbelievers in Me. He who said: We have had this rainfall due to the grace and mercy of Allah — is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the stars. And he who said we had rainfall due to a certain star — is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the stars.'
reasoning_span: Al-Bukhari recorded that Allah's Messenger ﷺ led the Subh (Dawn) prayer after it had rained during the night, then he said: «قَالَ: أَصْبَحَ مِنْ عِبَادِي مُؤْمِنٌ بِي وَكَافِرٌ، فَأَمَّا مَنْ قَالَ: مُطِرْنَا بِفَضْلِ اللهِ وَرَحْمَتِهِ فَذَاكَ مُؤْمِنٌ بِي كَافِرٌ بِالْكَوْكَبِ، وَأَمَّا مَنْ قَالَ: مُطِرْنَا بِنَوْءِ كَذَا وَكَذَا فَذَاكَ كَافِرٌ بِي مُؤْمِنٌ بِالْكَوْكَب»

question: According to Surah 10:44, what does Allah say about wronging people?
answer: Allah says: 'Truly, Allah wrongs not mankind in aught; but mankind wrong themselves.' This is because Allah is Just and does not oppress anyone; rather people oppress themselves through their own deeds.
reasoning_span: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يَظْلِمُ النَّاسَ شَيْئًا وَلَـكِنَّ النَّاسَ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ (Truly, Allah wrongs not mankind in aught; but mankind wrong themselves.)

question: What does the Prophet's hadith (Qudsi) say Allah has forbidden for Himself, in the tafsir of Surah 10:44?
answer: The hadith states: 'O My servant! I have prohibited oppression for Myself and made it prohibited for you, so do not oppress one another.' And at the end: 'O My servants! It is but your deeds that I reckon for you and then recompense you for. So let him who finds good praise Allah. And let him who finds other than that blame no one but himself.'
reasoning_span: «يَا عِبَادِي إِنِّي حَرَّمْتُ الظُّلْمَ عَلَى نَفْسِي وَجَعَلْتُهُ بَيْنَكُمْ مُحَرَّمًا فَلَا تَظَالَمُوا» (O My servant! I have prohibited oppression for Myself and made it prohibited for you, so do not oppress one another...)

question: What story about Ya'qub (Jacob) smelling Yusuf's (Joseph's) shirt is mentioned in the tafsir of Surah 12:95?
answer: When the caravan departed from Egypt, a wind brought the scent of Yusuf's shirt to Ya'qub. According to Ibn Abbas's narration through Sufyan Ath-Thawri, Ya'qub found Yusuf's scent from a distance of eight days away.
reasoning_span: "When the caravan departed from Egypt, a wind started blowing and brought the scent of Yusuf's shirt to Ya`qub. He said, إِنِّى لأَجِدُ رِيحَ يُوسُفَ لَوْلاَ أَن تُفَنِّدُونِ (I do indeed feel the smell of Yusuf , if only you think me not senile.) He found his scent from a distance of eight days away!"

question: What did Ya'qub's sons say when he claimed to smell Yusuf, in the tafsir of Surah 12:95?
answer: They said: 'Certainly, you are in your old Dalal (error/misguidance).' Qatadah commented that they meant his love for Yusuf had caused him to never forget him, and they uttered a harsh word to their father that they should never have uttered to him or to a Prophet of Allah.
reasoning_span: إِنَّكَ لَفِى ضَلَـلِكَ الْقَدِيمِ (Certainly, you are in your old Dalal.) meaning, `in your old error,' according to Ibn `Abbas. Qatadah commented, "They meant that, `because of your love for Yusuf you will never forget him.' So they uttered a harsh word to their father that they should never have uttered to him, nor to a Prophet of Allah."

question: According to Surah 53:36, what does the tafsir say about the scriptures of Moses and Ibrahim's fulfillment?
answer: The tafsir states that Ibrahim 'fulfilled' means he conveyed all that he was ordered to convey, delivered all that Allah ordered him to deliver, obeyed Allah, and delivered His Message to His creatures. This made him worthy of being made a leader for mankind.
reasoning_span: Sa`id bin Jubayr and Ath-Thawri said it means: "Conveyed all that he was ordered to convey." Ibn `Abbas said about: وَفَّى (fulfilled) "He delivered all that Allah ordered him to deliver."

question: What does Surah 53:36 say about each soul bearing another's burden?
answer: The tafsir states: 'No burdened person shall bear the burden of another.' Every soul shall carry its own injustices (whether disbelief or sin) and none else shall carry its burden of sin.
reasoning_span: أَلاَّ تَزِرُ وَزِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَى (That no burdened person shall bear the burden of another.) Meaning, every soul shall carry its own injustices, whether disbelief or sin, and none else shall carry its burden of sin

question: What does the tafsir of Surah 60:5 say about Ibrahim's prayer for his father?
answer: Ibrahim's prayer for his father was only a promise he had made. When it became clear to Ibrahim that his father was an enemy of Allah, he declared himself innocent of him. This is why believers cannot use Ibrahim's example as proof that they may pray for forgiveness for those who died on Shirk.
reasoning_span: إِلاَّ قَوْلَ إِبْرَهِيمَ لاًّبِيهِ لاّسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ (except the saying of Ibrahim to his father: "Verily, I will ask forgiveness (from Allah) for you...") means, `you have a good example in Ibrahim and his people; as for Ibrahim's prayers for Allah his father, it was a promise that he made for his father.' When Ibrahim became sure that his father was an enemy of Allah, he declared himself innocent of him.

question: What is 'Slanderer' (Hammaz) according to Ibn Abbas and Qatadah in the tafsir of Surah 68:11?
answer: According to Ibn Abbas and Qatadah, Hammaz means slander.
reasoning_span: هَمَّازٍ (A Hammaz, ) Ibn `Abbas and Qatadah both said, "This is slander."

question: What hadith from the Two Sahihs is mentioned about Namimah (tale-carrying) in the tafsir of Surah 68:11?
answer: It is confirmed in the Two Sahihs that Ibn Abbas said: 'The Messenger of Allah once passed by two graves and he said: Verily, these two are being punished. One of them was not careful about protecting himself from urine when relieving himself. The other one used to spread Namimah.'
reasoning_span: It is confirmed in the Two Sahihs that Mujahid reported from Tawus that Ibn `Abbas said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once passed by two graves and he said, «إِنَّهُمَا لَيُعَذَّبَانِ وَمَا يُعَذَّبَانِ فِي كَبِيرٍ، أَمَّا أَحَدُهُمَا فَكَانَ لَا يَسْتَتِرُ مِنَ الْبَوْلِ، وَأَمَّا الْاخَرُ فَكَانَ يَمْشِي بِالنَّمِيمَة» (Verily, these two are being punished, and they are not being punished for something major. One of them was not careful about protecting himself from urine (when relieving himself). The other one used to spread Namimah.)

question: What will happen to those who disbelieved when they are driven to Hell, according to Surah 39:71?
answer: They will be driven to Hell in groups. When they arrive, the gates of Hell will be opened and its keepers will ask: 'Did not the Messengers come to you from yourselves, reciting to you the Ayat of your Lord, and warning you of the meeting of this Day?' They will confess that they did, and say the word of torment was justified against the disbelievers.
reasoning_span: حَتَّى إِذَا جَآءُوهَا فُتِحَتْ أَبْوَبُهَا (till when they reach it, the gates thereof will be opened.) means, as soon as they arrive, the gates will be opened quickly, in order to hasten on their punishment. Then the keepers of Hell... will say to them by way of rebuking and reprimanding: أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّنكُمْ (Did not the Messengers come to you from yourselves,)

question: According to the tafsir of Surah 102:6, what does Al-Bukhari record about following the deceased?
answer: Al-Bukhari recorded from Anas bin Malik that the Prophet said: 'Three things follow the deceased person, and two of them return while one remains behind with him. The things which follow him are his family, his wealth and his deeds. His family and his wealth return while his deeds remain.'
reasoning_span: Al-Bukhari recorded from Anas bin Malik that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, «يَتْبَعُ الْمَيِّتَ ثَلَاثَةٌ، فَيَرْجِعُ اثْنَانِ وَيَبْقَى مَعَهُ وَاحِدٌ: يَتْبَعُهُ أَهْلُهُ وَمَالُهُ وَعَمَلُهُ، فَيَرْجِعُ أَهْلُهُ وَمَالُهُ، وَيَبْقَى عَمَلُه» (Three things follow the deceased person, and two of them return while one remains behind with him. The things which follow him are his family, his wealth and his deeds. His family and his wealth return while his deeds remain.)

question: What does the tafsir of Surah 43:51 say about Pharaoh's address to his people about the rivers of Egypt?
answer: Pharaoh assembled his people and boasted of his dominion, asking: 'Is not mine the dominion of Egypt, and these rivers flowing underneath me?' Qatadah said they had gardens and rivers of flowing water. Pharaoh was implying that Musa and his followers were poor and weak.
reasoning_span: Allah tells us how Fir`awn stubbornly persisted in his rebellion and disbelief. He assembled his people and addressed them in a vainglorious fashion, boasting of his dominion over Egypt. أَلَيْسَ لِى مُلْكُ مِصْرَ وَهَـذِهِ الاٌّنْهَـرُ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِى (Is not mine the dominion of Egypt, and these rivers flowing underneath me) Qatadah said, "They had gardens and rivers of flowing water."

question: What happens to believers when they enter Paradise according to the tafsir of Surah 39:71 and related verses?
answer: The gates of Paradise will be opened for them, and angels will greet them saying 'Peace be upon you! You have done well, so enter here to abide therein forever.' They will be greeted with words of welcome and honor.
reasoning_span: These words are not attributed to any specific person, but they are said as an indication that the entire universe will bear witness that they deserve what they are suffering, in accordance with the judgement of the Most Just, the All-Knowing.

question: What is 'Dari'' (the plant) described as in the tafsir of Surah 88:6?
answer: Dari' is a tree from the Hellfire. The people of the Hijaz call it Ad-Dari' when it dries, and Ash-Shibriq (or Ash-Shabraq). It is a thorny tree, poisonous, that provides neither nourishment nor relief from hunger.
reasoning_span: Al-Bukhari related that Mujahid said, "Ad-Dari` is a plant that is called Ash-Shibriq. The people of the Hijaz call it Ad-Dari` when it dries, and it is poisonous."... لاَّ يُسْمِنُ وَلاَ يُغْنِى مِن جُوعٍ (Which will neither nourish nor avail against hunger.)

question: According to the tafsir of Surah 83:21, where are the souls of the righteous (Al-Abrar) located?
answer: Their record (and final destination) is in 'Illiyyin, which is located in the seventh heaven, or according to some at Sidrat Al-Muntaha. The word Illiyyin is derived from Uluw (highness).
reasoning_span: The obvious meaning is that the word `Illiyyin is taken from the word `Uluw, which means highness. The more something ascends and rises, the more it becomes greater and increases... `Illiyyin is located at Sidrat Al-Muntaha.

question: What did Qatadah say about As-Sahirah in the context of Surah 79:43?
answer: Qatadah and others said that As-Sahirah means 'the face of the earth.' Ar-Rabi' bin Anas related it to the verse about the earth being changed to another earth on the Day of Resurrection.
reasoning_span: `Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd have all said, "As-Sahirah means the face of the earth."

question: What did the Romans and Persians do regarding breastfeeding, according to the tafsir of Surah 81?
answer: The Prophet observed that the Romans and Persians had sexual relations with their women who were breastfeeding their children, and this did not harm the children at all.
reasoning_span: «لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ أَنْهَى عَنِ الْغِيلَةِ فَنَظَرْتُ فِي الرُّومِ وَفَارِسَ، فَإِذَا هُمْ يُغِيلُونَ أَوْلَادَهُمْ، وَلَا يَضُرُّ أَوْلَادَهُمْ ذلِكَ شَيْئًا» (I was about to prohibit sexual relations with breast feeding women, but then I saw that the Romans and the Persians have sexual relations with their women who breast feed their children and it does not harm the children at all.)

question: According to the tafsir of Surah 79, what does Surah An-Nazi'at say about the angels who pull out souls?
answer: Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Masruq, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Abu Salih, Abu Ad-Duha and As-Suddi all said: 'By those who pull out, drowning — these are the angels who remove the souls from the Children of Adam.' Among them are those whose souls are removed with difficulty as if being drowned, and those whose souls are removed with ease.
reasoning_span: Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn `Abbas, Masruq, Sa`id bin Jubayr, Abu Salih, Abu Ad-Duha and As-Suddi all said, وَالنَّـزِعَـتِ غَرْقاً (By those who pull out, drowning.) "These are the angels who remove the souls from the Children of Adam." Among them are those whose souls are removed by the angels with difficulty, as if he is being drowned during its removal.

question: What does the tafsir of Surah 30:5 say about why the Romans' victory was important to Muslims?
answer: The Muslims wanted the Romans to prevail over the Persians because the Romans were People of the Book, and the idolators wanted the Persians to prevail because the Persians were idol worshippers (Zoroastrian fire worshippers).
reasoning_span: The idolators wanted the Persians to prevail over the Romans, because they were idol worshippers, and the Muslims wanted the Romans to prevail over the Persians, because they were People of the Book.

question: What did Abu Bakr agree on as the time limit for the bet about the Romans defeating the Persians?
answer: Abu Bakr and the idolators agreed on six years as the limit. The idolators said Bid' (few) meant between three and nine years, so they agreed on six years as the middle. Six years passed without the Romans being victorious, and the idolators took the bet. Then in the seventh year the Romans were victorious.
reasoning_span: they said to Abu Bakr: `What do you think, Bid` means something between three and nine years, so let us agree on the middle.' So they agreed on six years. Then six years passed without the Romans being victorious, so the idolators took what they had bet with Abu Bakr. When the seventh year came and the Romans were finally victorious over the Persians

question: What does the parable in Surah 30:28 about slaves being partners teach about monotheism?
answer: The parable shows that just as no one would like to have their slave as an equal partner in their wealth (fearing that the slave would share equally), it is even less fitting for Allah to have partners. If humans abhor such a thing among themselves, they should not attribute rivals to Allah from among His creation.
reasoning_span: This is the parable Allah makes of the idolators, those who worship others besides Him and attribute partners to Him... `None of you would like to have his servant as a partner in his wealth, each of them having an equal share.' Abu Mijlaz said, "You do not fear that your servant will have a share in your wealth with you, because he has no such right; similarly, Allah has no partner."

question: In the story of the garden owners in Surah 68:30, what did the most just among them say they should have done?
answer: The most just among them (Awsat) said: 'Did I not tell you, why do you not Tusabbihun (say If Allah wills)?'
reasoning_span: قَالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَّكُمْ لَوْلاَ تُسَبِّحُونَ (The Awsat among them said,) Ibn `Abbas, Mujahid, Sa`id bin Jubayr, `Ikrimah, Muhammad bin Ka`b, Ar-Rabi` bin Anas, Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah all said, "This means the most just of them and the best of them." أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَّكُمْ لَوْلاَ تُسَبِّحُونَ (Did I not tell you, `Why do you not Tusabbihun') Mujahid, As-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj all said that, لَوْلاَ تُسَبِّحُونَ (Why do you not Tusabbihun) this means "why do you not say, `If Allah wills'"

question: What does the tafsir of Surah 15:32 say about Iblees's reason for refusing to prostrate to Adam?
answer: Iblees refused out of envy, disbelief, stubbornness, arrogance, and false pride. He said: 'I am not one to prostrate myself to a human, whom You created from dried (sounding) clay of altered mud.' He argued that he was better than Adam because he was created from fire while Adam was created from clay.
reasoning_span: Allah informs us of how He mentioned Adam to His angels before He created him, and how He honored him by commanding the angels to prostrate to him. He mentions how His enemy Iblis, amidst all the angels, refused to prostrate to him out of envy, disbelief, stubbornness, arrogance, and false pride. This is why Iblis said: لَمْ أَكُن لاًّسْجُدَ لِبَشَرٍ خَلَقْتَهُ مِن صَلْصَـلٍ مِّنْ حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ (I am not one to prostrate myself to a human, whom You created from dried (sounding) clay of altered mud.)

question: What does the tafsir say about Ibrahim's (Abraham's) declaration of Tawhid to his people in Surah 43:28?
answer: Ibrahim declared: 'Verily, I am innocent of what you worship, except Him Who created me; and verily, He will guide me.' He made this a word lasting among his offspring — the word La ilaha illallah (worship of Allah Alone), which his guided descendants would continue to say.
reasoning_span: Ibrahim declared: وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَهِيمُ لاًّبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِى بَرَآءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ - إِلاَّ الَّذِى فَطَرَنِى فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ ("Verily, I am innocent of what you worship, except Him Who created me; and verily, He will guide me.") The Word means the worship of Allah Alone with no partner or associate, and the denunciation of all gods apart from Him, i.e., La ilaha illallah.

question: What does the tafsir of Surah 9:8 say about the idolators' covenant?
answer: The tafsir states that the idolators do not deserve a covenant of peace because of their Shirk and disbelief. If they had a chance to defeat Muslims, they would cause great mischief, disregard the ties of kinship and the sanctity of their vows, and not observe any pact of kinship or covenant of protection.
reasoning_span: Allah encourages the believers to show enmity to the idolators and to dissociate from them, affirming that they do not deserve to enjoy a covenant of peace, because of their Shirk in Allah and disbelief in Allah's Messenger If these disbelievers have a chance to defeat Muslims, they will cause great mischief, leave nothing unharmed, disregard the ties of kinship and the sanctity of their vows.

question: What does the tafsir of Surah 90:19 say about those who disbelieve in Allah's signs?
answer: Those who disbelieve in Allah's signs are the companions of the Left Hand, and upon them is Fire that will be Mu'sadah (sealed/shut), meaning it will be sealed over them with no way to avoid it, no way out, no light, no crevice, and no escape from it forever.
reasoning_span: وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـَايَـتِنَا هُمْ أَصْحَـبُ الْمَشْـَمَةِ (But those who disbelieve in Our Ayat, they are those on the Left.) meaning, the companions of the Left Hand. عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُّؤْصَدَةُ (Upon them Fire will Mu'sadah.) meaning, it will be sealed over them and there will be no way for them to avoid it, nor will they have any way out.
